subject: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kennedy <sara.kennedy@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing

Team —

Following the kickoff with Acme Health last week, they are asking for two paths to production: a VPC-hosted private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering + KMS) and an on-prem appliance option for one of their air-gapped data centers. They want a feasibility readout by the end of next week so sales can commit to timelines. Can we scope architecture risks, required infra changes, and rough FTEs for engineering + security support?

High-level asks from Acme (attached):
- VPC: direct peering + private IP routing, customer KMS integration, audit log forwarding to their SIEM, per-tenant network isolation.
- On-prem: dockerized runtime bundle, admin UI for local management, offline model artifact install flow, support window SLA.

Immediate goals for this thread:
1) Call out blockers in architecture (network, auth, storage).
2) Estimate engineering lift (development + QA + infra) in quarter-month buckets.
3) List compliance/security gating items we cannot meet without product changes.

Dev / Hiro / Evelyn — please reply with your initial notes. I put Laura on Cc for visibility on timelines / commercial implications.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kennedy <sara.kennedy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing

Thanks Marissa — quick read from an architecture/dev perspective.

VPC-hosted private deployment (customer VPC peering):
- Feasible with current runtime but requires:
  - Private networking stack changes to allow mTLS over private IPs and support for customer-managed DNS overrides (2-3 sprints).
  - KMS integration: we have our KMS adapter but need customer KMS onboarding flow + key rotation UX (1 sprint backend + 1 sprint console).
  - Audit log forwarding: generic syslog/HTTP webhook forwarder exists; need mapping to their SIEM schema and retention config (1 sprint).
- Storage: KV cache and model artifacts can remain in our managed S3-equivalent; however Acme may require on-prem model artifact hosting for the on-prem option.

On-prem appliance: larger lift. Main blockers:
- Runtime packaging: we can containerize the inference runtime but must decouple control plane dependencies (3-4 sprints).
- Model artifact signing & offline install mechanism (2 sprints).
- Licensing / telemetry: customer wants limited telemetry; need configurable telemetry toggles + offline usage reporting (2 sprints).
- Ops support: will require runbook + remote-support tooling (1 sprint) and a small dedicated support rotation for the first six months.

Rough resourcing (engineering only):
- VPC path: 1 PM (part-time), 2 Backend Eng (4 sprints), 1 Infra Eng (2 sprints), 1 QA (2 sprints).
- On-Prem path: 1 PM (half-time), 3 Backend Eng (6 sprints), 2 Infra/Release Eng (4 sprints), 2 QA (6 sprints).

Open questions for Acme / Security:
- Do they accept our managed model storage for VPC or must all artifacts live in their environment?
- Telemetry restrictions for on-prem (need exact list of forbidden metrics).

I can put a detailed task breakdown into JIRA-INF-4128 if you want.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sara Kennedy <sara.kennedy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing

Adding infra constraints / deployment ops perspective.

VPC path specifics:
- Network: We'll need to support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink style endpoints (depends on customer's cloud). Estimate: 2 infra-focused sprints to add PrivateLink + peering orchestration templates.
- HA and scaling: For dedicated VPC deployments we must size for their peak QPS and ensure autoscaling hooks are compatible with private networking (1 sprint to validate).
- Billing/metrics: route usage tranche reporting to our billing pipeline; may need tagging and per-tenant rate limiting (1 sprint).

On-prem specifics:
- Hardware footprint: conservative starting spec: 4 x A100 equivalent nodes for medium throughput (we can produce a sizing matrix).
- Installation: need an installer script + preflight checks (storage/memory/ports) and an offline bundle (1-2 sprints infra + 2 sprints release engineering to harden).
- Security controls: kernel-level isolation not required but we should recommend container runtime constraints and SELinux/AppArmor profiles (security to confirm).

Support model: recommend offering a 12-week onboarding bundle (professional services engagement) plus an optional annual support SLA. This requires one dedicated release engineer and one infra engineer allocated for the onboarding period.

I'll attach a capacity estimate spreadsheet (attached).

-Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Lead Infrastructure Engineer

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kennedy <sara.kennedy@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing

Security & compliance perspective — initial triage.

VPC:
- KMS integration is acceptable if we can perform key proofing and audit of key usage. We need a defined key-rotation policy and the ability to produce key usage logs to their KMS.
- Network egress: we must ensure no unexpected egress to public internet for customer workloads; require strict egress policies and validation testing.
- Data residency: confirm whether model telemetry or cached prompts are considered PHI/PII; Acme Health flagged some PII concerns in the doc. If so, we need contractual CLAs and possibly an isolated storage option.

On-Prem:
- Cryptographic assurances: require signed model bundles and verification tooling. We also need to confirm what encryption-at-rest approach they need for local artifact storage.
- Audit & forensic: customer requires 90-day immutable audit logs for security-relevant actions; implementing this in an offline environment is non-trivial but possible with local logging + signed log rotation. Expect 2 sprints of work to provide a certified log export format.

Hard blocker: SOC2 requirement for handling patient data. If Acme insists that any PHI transit the appliance, we must treat it as a HIPAA workload and bring legal + compliance into the loop. That will delay timelines by multiple weeks.

Next steps from security:
- Marissa, please confirm whether Acme will route PHI through the appliance or whether the on-prem box will only handle non-PHI workloads.
- We should schedule a scoped security questionnaire review with Acme next week (I can lead).

-Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Feasibility review: Private (VPC) & On-Prem deployment — architecture and resourcing

Quick summary and proposed delivery plan for the Sales thread: 

Summary:
- VPC option: technically feasible with ~6-8 sprint-equivalents of cross-team work (Dev + Infra + Security + QA). No major architectural rewrites; mostly integration work.
- On-Prem option: medium-risk, larger lift (~12-16 sprints) across runtime packaging, release engineering, signed artifact flows, and onboarding delivery. Requires PS engagement.
- Blocking security item: PHI/HIPAA classification could add legal & compliance gating; need confirmation from Acme.

Proposed next steps (owners / ETA):
1) Marissa: Confirm PHI routing with Acme and capture exact telemetry constraints (by 2026-03-11).
2) Dev: Create JIRA task breakdown under JIRA-INF-4128 and estimate story points (by 2026-03-12).
3) Hiro: Provide hard hardware sizing matrix and installer preflight checklist (by 2026-03-12).
4) Evelyn: Run a focused security questionnaire session with Acme; produce a list of mandatory controls (by 2026-03-13).
5) Laura: Pricing / PS packaging for on-prem (by 2026-03-15).

Sara — can you confirm whether the on-prem box will ever handle PHI? If yes, please flag and we will escalate to Legal.

I'll follow up with a concise PLA (project-level agreement) doc and a proposed timeline for sales to share with Acme.

Thanks everyone — please reply inline if you disagree with owners / ETAs.

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
